drhp.business: Chartered Logistics Limited is an asset-light-to-asset-medium Indian logistics company offering road transportation, cost-and-freight solutions and special warehousing from point of origin to final destination. It serves industrial shippers nationwide through a mix of owned and attached vehicles, with GPS-enabled tracking and real-time delivery updates built into the service. The business is a pure services operation — the Company states it is neither involved in any manufacturing nor processing activities.

risks.note: Called out by management as one of the primary challenges of the sector, directly affecting operating costs and profit margins; the Managing Director separately attributes FY26 pressure to increased diesel prices through the year with rising overheads. For a road-transport operator with an owned-and-attached fleet this is the single largest uncontrollable input cost.

The sector faces an acute shortage of trained drivers, warehouse operators and logistics managers, which affects service scalability and reliability; the MD's letter names driver shortage and labour shortage among the problems the Company had to face during the year.

Inflationary pressures and fluctuations in interest and exchange rates create an unpredictable business environment. Finance cost is material enough that the Company's stated mitigation is to watch the money market continuously to bring the cost of finance to the lowest possible level.
risks.risk: Interest rate, inflation and exchange-rate movement

risks.note: Congested highways, underdeveloped rural connectivity and limited multimodal integration hinder logistics efficiency — causing delays, raising maintenance costs and reducing service quality.
Rising frequency of floods, cyclones and heatwaves poses environmental risk that disrupts operations and damages assets — a direct hazard to a vehicle fleet and to cargo in transit.

Increasing reliance on digital systems exposes the business to hacking, ransomware and data breaches, which can compromise critical business systems, disrupt delivery timelines and harm stakeholder trust.

Stricter norms on emissions, data protection and transport safety; non-compliance can lead to financial penalties, reputational damage and operational restrictions. The Company's own FY26 record shows this is live: the Secretarial Auditor flagged delayed filing of a disclosure under Regulation 31(4) of the SEBI Takeover Regulations and belated Structured Digital Database entries, and BSE issued a notice on incorrect submission of the SDD compliance certificate for the quarter ended June 2025.

The growing presence of tech-enabled logistics start-ups is intensifying competitive pressure, compelling traditional players to innovate continuously to retain market share — a structural threat to a conventional fleet-based operator.

currentContext.expansion: The annual report describes no named capex project, commissioning timeline or capacity addition. Expansion is stated only as intent: the Company is evaluating potential expansions in warehousing, 3PL and cold chain logistics to diversify its service portfolio, and is exploring partnerships to enter high-growth verticals like cold chain logistics and last-mile delivery. The only capability build-out described is technology-led — deployment of GPS tracking, fleet management systems and data analytics for route and load optimisation, which management says has already enabled better visibility, customer responsiveness and cost efficiency — plus assessment of cleaner fuel alternatives, optimised vehicle usage and environmentally conscious vehicle upgrades to reduce the carbon footprint. On the entity side the Company acquired a 99.99% stake in Chartered Comcare IFSC Limited (acquired 12 August 2024), which as at 31 March 2026 had not commenced revenue-generating activity. No rupee capex quantum, no project name and no completion or ramp date is disclosed anywhere in this bundle.
